caption: Two cars costing the same as the bond bothers me. Do couples really split these 50/50 or is that just us?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R34 500
household income
Living in Lephalale
slides.body:
Him 30, her 28
Married, baby due in four months
Jobs: Scaffolder at the power station & clinic receptionist
Combined net income: R34 500 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.body: We bought two years ago when it felt cheap. With a baby coming I check that number more often.

slides.title: Cars
slides.body: His is a Hilux for site, mine is a Picanto. They cost almost the same. I don't like that.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.body: He eats like a scaffolder. I eat like a pregnant person. The trolley is a negotiation.

slides.title: Medical aid
slides.body: We upgraded the plan for the birth. It added R1 200 and I'm trying not to look at it.

slides.title: Family support
slides.includes: His mother in Mokopane, my sister's rent
slides.body: Split 50/50. We agreed on it before we got married, which helped.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Funeral policies, stokvel, prepaid electricity, water, fibre, phones, baby fund, DStv
slides.body: R600 of that goes into a baby fund. The stokvel pays out in December and I'm already planning around it.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R34 500. On paper it's fine. The nursery is still a spare room full of boxes.

slides.title: We stopped guessing
slides.body:
We uploaded our statements to Beyond Horizon and it listed every recurring debit order.

We'd forgotten about two.

No bank login needed.
